proposed.statement:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\).  Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\).  Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the sharp target-cell range is the attained interval
\[
\left[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star),
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\right].
\]
It is strictly inside \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and it is a singleton exactly when the cell is identified.  Distinct minimizers and maximizers give original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining the endpoints.  These are finite semialgebraic characterizations; effective exact decision is claimed only when the menu probabilities have an effective rational or algebraic encoding.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform.  In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division.  If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the sharp conditional range is the attained interval
\[
\left[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)},
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\right].
\]
Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive.  Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
For a sparse nonsaturated graph or a cross-district-coupled menu, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is only an outer relaxation.  Equality for the saturated fiber follows only under \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) by the one-district fiber-projection theorem.  Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside that theorem's scope; distinct optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate.

payload.reason: State exact multi-affine saturated and exact graph-compatible sparse frontiers side by side, with finite semialgebraic rather than unconditional algorithmic claims.

payload.current:
Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\).  The set \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set of finite dimension, and canonical realization on the declared observed alphabets gives, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
 \bigl\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):
       \mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
 =
 \bigl\{(\Phi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
       \theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\bigr\}.
\]
Consequently, the extrema \(L_T(\mathcal P)\) and \(U_T(\mathcal P)\) are attained and are the sharp bounds for every target cell \(T\).  The bounds are strictly tighter than the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when \(L_T(\mathcal P)>0\) or \(U_T(\mathcal P)<1\), an exactly checkable property of the displayed program.  The cell is identified if and only if \(L_T(\mathcal P)=U_T(\mathcal P)\); if \(L_T(\mathcal P)<U_T(\mathcal P)\), minimizing and maximizing canonical parameters yield two SCM families on the original observed alphabets that agree on every cell of every complete supplied law and disagree on \(T\).

Let
\[
 e_-=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star),
 \qquad
 e_+=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star).
\]
If \(e_+ =0\), the evidence has probability zero throughout the compatibility fiber; if \(e_-=0<e_+\), its positivity is not uniform.  In both cases a conditional functional on the entire fiber is rejected before division.  If \(e_->0\), the sharp range of the conditional arm value is
\[
 \left[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)},
 \quad
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)}
 \right],
\]
with both endpoints attained.  Under the same condition \(e_->0\), uniform strict ordering satisfies
\[
 \begin{array}{rcl}
 Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)>0,\\[3pt]
 Q_\rho^\star>Q_\sigma^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0,
 \end{array}
\]
and two original-alphabet compatible families with opposite strict rankings exist if and only if
\[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0
 <\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta).
\]
In particular, a target structural-causal bandit may safely prune \(\rho\) in favor of \(\sigma\) exactly when the first strict minimum condition holds.

For every district \(D\), the global projection satisfies
\[
 \{q_D^\star(\cdot;\theta^\star):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}
 \subseteq \mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
A local point, or a pair of local points, lifts to globally compatible SCM families exactly when it belongs, or they both belong, to the left-hand projection.  Equality with \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) follows under the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem, but is not implied in a multi-district problem.  Hence a local \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) face-failure trace alone is not a global paired-model certificate; the exact multi-district certificate is instead furnished by distinct optimizers of the displayed global polynomial programs.

\[
b_D=\lambda^\top A_D+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\]

On that saturated separated class, failure yields two compatible SCM families on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\) that agree on every supplied law and disagree on the target cell.  For a nonsaturated or cross-district-coupled problem, failure is only a local outer-relaxation witness.

proposed.construction: Define \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}\) to contain exactly the families in \(\mathfrak M\) for which every \(G[D]\) is bidirected complete and, in every domain, one latent response variable \(U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\) generates all mechanisms in \(D\) by reading the component maps of \(U_D^s\).
